claim: Polo-like kinase 4 (PLK4) is the master regulator of centriole biogenesis and is required for centriole assembly in all cycling mammalian cell types studied.
source: Polo-like kinase 4 (PLK4) is the master regulator of centriole biogenesis and is required for centriole assembly in all cycling mammalian cell types studied (Bettencourt-Dias et al., 2005; Habedanck et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research (Bettencourt-Dias et al., 2005; Habedanck et al., 2005).

claim: During centriole duplication, CEP152 and CEP192 recruit PLK4 to the surface of the parent centrioles.
source: During centriole duplication, CEP152 and CEP192 recruit PLK4 to the surface of the parent centrioles (Cizmecioglu et al., 2010; Hatch et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2013; Sonnen et al., 2013; Park et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: PLK4 kinase activity directs the assembly of STIL and SAS6 into a central cartwheel that provides the structural foundation for the new procentriole.
source: PLK4 kinase activity directs the assembly of STIL and SAS6 into a central cartwheel that provides the structural foundation for the new procentriole, and inhibition of PLK4 activity blocks centriole assembly (Dzhindzhev et al., 2014; Ohta et al., 2014; Kratz et al., 2015; Moyer et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Inhibition of PLK4 activity blocks centriole assembly.
source: PLK4 kinase activity directs the assembly of STIL and SAS6 into a central cartwheel that provides the structural foundation for the new procentriole, and inhibition of PLK4 activity blocks centriole assembly (Dzhindzhev et al., 2014; Ohta et al., 2014; Kratz et al., 2015; Moyer et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: PLK4 is recruited to the surface of both parent centrioles and deuterosomes in MCCs.
source: PLK4 is recruited to the surface of both parent centrioles and deuterosomes in MCCs (Nanjundappa et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Inhibiting PLK4 kinase activity with centrinone has no impact on centriole amplification in mouse multiciliated ependymal cells or mTECs.
source: However, recent work has shown that inhibiting PLK4 kinase activity with the ATP-competitive small molecule centrinone has no impact on centriole amplification in mouse multiciliated ependymal cells or mTECs (Nanjundappa et al., 2019; Zhao et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: shRNA-mediated depletion of PLK4 modestly delays centriole assembly in mTECs but does not reduce the final number of centrioles produced or the fraction of cells forming motile cilia.
source: In addition, shRNA-mediated depletion of PLK4 modestly delays centriole assembly in mTECs but does not reduce the final number of centrioles produced or the fraction of cells forming motile cilia (Nanjundappa et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: PLK4 levels are upregulated ~20-fold in differentiating mTECs.
source: However, PLK4 levels are upregulated ~20-fold in differentiating mTECs, and it remains plausible that partial inhibition or depletion of PLK4 is not sufficient to prevent centriole amplification in MCCs (Hoh et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Cre-mediated excision of exon 5 generates a Plk4 allele lacking a large portion of the PLK4 kinase domain, including the DFG motif required for kinase activity.
source: Cre-mediated excision of exon 5 generates a Plk4 allele (hereafter Plk4Δ allele) lacking a large portion of the PLK4 kinase domain, including the DFG motif required for kinase activity.
evidence: The claim is based on the design of the genetic construct described in the manuscript.

claim: Splicing of Plk4 exon 4 into exon 6 is predicted to generate a frameshift that creates a premature termination codon at amino acid 119.
source: Splicing of Plk4 exon 4 into exon 6 is predicted to generate a frameshift that creates a premature termination codon at amino acid 119 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on the predicted outcome of the genetic modification and is supported by a figure.

claim: Intercrosses of Plk4F/Δ mice produced Plk4F/F and Plk4F/Δ progeny but Plk4Δ/Δ animals were never observed.
source: Intercrosses of Plk4F/Δ mice produced Plk4F/F and Plk4F/Δ progeny but Plk4Δ/Δ animals were never observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Plk4F/F;NestinCre animals developed severe microcephaly leading to a 35% reduction in telencephalic area at E14.5.
source: Plk4F/F;NestinCre animals developed severe microcephaly leading to a 35% reduction in telencephalic area at E14.5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Loss of PLK4 led to a dramatic decrease in centriole number in dividing neural progenitor cells at the ventricular zone in E14.5 cortices.
source: As expected, loss of PLK4 led to a dramatic decrease in centriole number (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Plk4F is a conditional loss-of-function allele of Plk4.
source: We conclude that Plk4F is a conditional loss-of-function allele of Plk4.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental validation of the genetic construct.

claim: The frequency of FOXJ1+ ependymal cells at each time point was similar in Plk4F/+ and Plk4F/F Cre+ cells.
source: The frequency of FOXJ1+ ependymal cells at each time point was similar in Plk4F/+ and Plk4F/F Cre+ cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Plk4F/F and Plk4F/+ cells formed deuterosomes at the same frequency.
source: In addition, Plk4F/F and Plk4F/+ cells formed deuterosomes at the same frequency (Figure 1C), indicating that loss of PLK4 does not block the differentiation of MCCs in vitro.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: Loss of PLK4 does not block the differentiation of MCCs in vitro.
source: In addition, Plk4F/F and Plk4F/+ cells formed deuterosomes at the same frequency (Figure 1C), indicating that loss of PLK4 does not block the differentiation of MCCs in vitro.
evidence: The claim is based on the interpretation of experimental data.

claim: PLK4 abundance was reduced by 80% in Cre+ Plk4F/F ependymal cells compared to Cre+ Plk4F/+ control cells.
source: PLK4 abundance was reduced by 80% in Cre+ Plk4F/F ependymal cells compared to Cre+ Plk4F/+control cells (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Deuterosomal recruitment of STIL was abolished in Cre-expressing Plk4F/F ependymal cells.
source: Consistent with PLK4 loss, deuterosomal recruitment of the PLK4 substrate and early centriole assembly factor STIL was abolished in Cre-expressing Plk4F/F ependymal cells (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: PLK4 is required to recruit STIL to the site of procentriole assembly in differentiating ependymal cells.
source: These data show that similar to cycling cells, PLK4 is required to recruit STIL to the site of procentriole assembly in differentiating ependymal cells.
evidence: The claim is based on the interpretation of experimental data.

claim: Cre+ Plk4F/+ ependymal cells amplified ~100 centrioles per cell.
source: Cre+ Plk4F/+ependymal cells amplified ~100 centrioles per cell, while most Plk4F/F ependymal cells failed to undergo centriole amplification and contained only the two parent centrioles that were present at the start of MCC differentiation (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Most Plk4F/F ependymal cells failed to undergo centriole amplification and contained only the two parent centrioles that were present at the start of MCC differentiation.
source: Cre+ Plk4F/+ependymal cells amplified ~100 centrioles per cell, while most Plk4F/F ependymal cells failed to undergo centriole amplification and contained only the two parent centrioles that were present at the start of MCC differentiation (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Cre+ FOXJ1+ Plk4F/F ependymal cells rarely nucleated multicilia.
source: Consistently, Cre+ FOXJ1+Plk4F/F ependymal cells rarely nucleated multicilia (Figure 2C and D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Procentrioles were absent in ependymal cells lacking PLK4.
source: We observed procentrioles associated with both deuterosomes and parent centrioles in control cells, but procentrioles were absent in ependymal cells lacking PLK4 (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by expansion microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: PLK4 is required for the earliest stages of centriole assembly in ependymal MCCs.
source: This confirms that PLK4 is required for the earliest stages of centriole assembly in ependymal MCCs.
evidence: The claim is based on the interpretation of experimental data.

claim: Loss of centrioles in NPCs activates a USP28-53BP1-TP53 mitotic surveillance pathway that blocks NPC proliferation and indirectly depletes MCCs.
source: Loss of centrioles in NPCs activates a USP28-53BP1-TP53 mitotic surveillance pathway that blocks NPC proliferation and indirectly depletes MCCs (Lambrus et al., 2016; Phan et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Plk4F/F;NestinCre mice died shortly after birth.
source: While Plk4F/F;NestinCre mice died shortly after birth, Plk4F/F;Usp28F/F;NestinCre animals survived past postnatal day 21.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation.

claim: Plk4F/F;Usp28F/F;NestinCre animals survived past postnatal day 21.
source: While Plk4F/F;NestinCre mice died shortly after birth, Plk4F/F;Usp28F/F;NestinCre animals survived past postnatal day 21.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation.

claim: FOXJ1+ ependymal cells in Plk4F/F;Usp28F/F;NestinCre brains lacked CEP164+ basal bodies and were devoid of multicilia.
source: FOXJ1+ ependymal cells could readily be identified in the lateral ventricles of Plk4F/F;Usp28F/F;NestinCre brains. However, these cells lacked CEP164+ basal bodies and were devoid of multicilia (Figure 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: PLK4 is required for centriole amplification in multiciliated ependymal cells in vitro and in vivo.
source: Taken together, these data show that PLK4 is required for centriole amplification in multiciliated ependymal cells in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: The claim is based on the interpretation of experimental data from multiple experiments.

claim: Comparable fractions of Plk4F/F;R26Cre and Plk4F/+;R26Cre mTECs expressed FOXJ1 at ALI 7 and ALI 21.
source: Comparable fractions of Plk4F/F;R26Cre and Plk4F/+;R26Cre mTECs expressed FOXJ1 at ALI 7 and ALI 21 and formed deuterosomes at ALI 3 and ALI 21 (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Plk4F/F;R26Cre and Plk4F/+;R26Cre mTECs formed deuterosomes at ALI 3 and ALI 21.
source: Comparable fractions of Plk4F/F;R26Cre and Plk4F/+;R26Cre mTECs expressed FOXJ1 at ALI 7 and ALI 21 and formed deuterosomes at ALI 3 and ALI 21 (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: CEP152 was recruited to deuterosomes in both Plk4F/F;R26Cre and control mTECs.
source: Similar to ependymal cells, CEP152 was recruited to deuterosomes in both Plk4F/F;R26Cre and control mTECs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: The percentage of cells with deuterosomes decreased from ~25% at ALI 3 to ~5% at ALI 21 in both control and Plk4F/F;R26Cre mTECs.
source: The percentage of cells with deuterosomes decreased from ~25% at ALI 3 to ~5% at ALI 21 in both control and Plk4F/F;R26Cre mTECs (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: mTECs lacking PLK4 undergo similar transitions to cells that amplify centrioles: first recruiting CEP152 to deuterosomes and later degrading/disassembling deuterosomes.
source: These data show that mTECs lacking PLK4 undergo similar transitions to cells that amplify centrioles: first recruiting CEP152 to deuterosomes and later degrading/disassembling deuterosomes.
evidence: The claim is based on the interpretation of experimental data.

claim: PLK4 localized to deuterosomes during the early stages of centriole amplification in control mTECs.
source: In control mTECs, PLK4 localized to deuterosomes during the early stages of centriole amplification.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation.

claim: Deuterosomal levels of PLK4 declined after centriole disengagement in control mTECs.
source: Deuterosomal levels of PLK4 declined after centriole disengagement, and weak PLK4 staining was retained on disengaged centrioles (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: About 55% of control mTECs exhibited PLK4 staining on deuterosomes at ALI 3.
source: About 55% of control mTECs exhibited PLK4 staining on deuterosomes at ALI 3, reflecting the percentage of DEUP1+ cells in the early stages of amplification.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: PLK4 was only present on deuterosomes in 15% of Plk4F/F;R26Cre mTECs at ALI 3.
source: However, PLK4 was only present on deuterosomes in 15% of Plk4F/F;R26Cre mTECs at ALI 3 (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The deuterosomal recruitment of the cartwheel proteins STIL and SAS6 was impaired in Plk4F/F;R26Cre mTECs.
source: Consistent with the loss of PLK4, the deuterosomal recruitment of the cartwheel proteins STIL and SAS6 was impaired in Plk4F/F;R26Cre mTECs (Figure 4F and G; Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: About 40% of control mTECs formed multiple cilia by ALI 7.
source: Moreover, while 40% of control mTECs formed multiple cilia, only 4% of PLK4F/F;R26Cre mTECs contained CEP164+ basal bodies and nucleated multiple cilia by ALI 7 (Figure 4H, I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Only 4% of PLK4F/F;R26Cre mTECs contained CEP164+ basal bodies and nucleated multiple cilia by ALI 7.
source: Moreover, while 40% of control mTECs formed multiple cilia, only 4% of PLK4F/F;R26Cre mTECs contained CEP164+ basal bodies and nucleated multiple cilia by ALI 7 (Figure 4H, I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: ~25% of both control and PLK4F/F;R26Cre mTECs expressed FOXJ1 at ALI 21.
source: Although ~25% of both control and PLK4F/F;R26Cre mTECs expressed FOXJ1 (Figure 4B), fewer than 5% of PLK4F/F;R26Cre mTECs underwent centriole amplification at ALI 21 (Figure 4J and K).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Fewer than 5% of PLK4F/F;R26Cre mTECs underwent centriole amplification at ALI 21.
source: Although ~25% of both control and PLK4F/F;R26Cre mTECs expressed FOXJ1 (Figure 4B), fewer than 5% of PLK4F/F;R26Cre mTECs underwent centriole amplification at ALI 21 (Figure 4J and K).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The small fraction of Plk4F/F;R26Cre cells that underwent centriole amplification are likely to have escaped Cre-mediated recombination and consequently express PLK4 at normal levels.
source: The small fraction of Plk4F/F;R26Cre cells that underwent centriole amplification are likely to have escaped Cre-mediated recombination and consequently express PLK4 at normal levels.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: PLK4 is required for centriole amplification in mTECs.
source: We conclude that PLK4 is also required for centriole amplification in mTECs.
evidence: The claim is based on the interpretation of experimental data.

claim: Control mTECs frequently formed irregularly shaped assemblies of Centrin at the early stages of centriole amplification.
source: Control mTECs frequently formed irregularly shaped assemblies of the distal centriole protein Centrin at the early stages of centriole amplification.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation.

claim: Irregularly shaped assemblies of Centrin were mostly absent in fully differentiated control MCCs.
source: However, these structures were mostly absent in fully differentiated MCCs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: 4OHT-treated Plk4F/F;R26Cre cells that failed centriole amplification formed large filamentous assemblies of Centrin.
source: By contrast, 4OHT-treated Plk4F/F;R26Cre cells that failed centriole amplification formed large filamentous assemblies of Centrin (hereafter PLK4 knockout) (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: In control mTECs, amplified procentrioles were stained with acetylated-α-tubulin to mark the centriole microtubule wall, and Centrin which resides in the lumen of the centriole.
source: In control mTECs, amplified procentrioles were stained with acetylated-α-tubulin to mark the centriole microtubule wall, and Centrin which resides in the lumen of the centriole (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by expansion microscopy data shown in a figure.

claim: In PLK4 knockout mTECs, acetylated-α-tubulin and Centrin marked the parent centrioles and the filamentous Centrin assemblies.
source: In PLK4 knockout mTECs, acetylated-α-tubulin and Centrin marked the parent centrioles (Figure 5D, arrows) and the filamentous Centrin assemblies.
evidence: The claim is supported by expansion microscopy data shown in a figure.

claim: Procentrioles were not observed in mTECs lacking PLK4.
source: Consistent with the observations in ependymal cells, procentrioles were not observed in mTECs lacking PLK4.
evidence: The claim is supported by expansion microscopy data.

claim: Centrin-GFP recovered by 23% over 10 min at the amplified centrioles of control mTECs.
source: While Centrin-GFP recovered by 23% over 10 min at the amplified centrioles of control mTECs, recovery was limited to 10% in the filamentous assemblies formed in mTECs lacking PLK4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Centrin-GFP recovery was limited to 10% in the filamentous assemblies formed in mTECs lacking PLK4.
source: While Centrin-GFP recovered by 23% over 10 min at the amplified centrioles of control mTECs, recovery was limited to 10% in the filamentous assemblies formed in mTECs lacking PLK4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The proximal centriole protein CEP135 formed large spherical assemblies in PLK4 knockout mTECs.
source: The proximal centriole protein CEP135 formed large spherical assemblies in PLK4 knockout mTECs.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation.

claim: CEP135 assemblies were distinct from the filamentous assemblies of Centrin observed in mTECs that fail centriole amplification.
source: These assemblies were distinct from the filamentous assemblies of Centrin observed in mTECs that fail centriole amplification (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: The distal centriole protein Centrobin formed ectopic assemblies in mTECs lacking PLK4.
source: The distal centriole protein Centrobin, the distal appendage component CEP164 and γTubulin also formed ectopic assemblies in mTECs lacking PLK4 (Figure 5E–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The distal appendage component CEP164 formed ectopic assemblies in mTECs lacking PLK4.
source: The distal centriole protein Centrobin, the distal appendage component CEP164 and γTubulin also formed ectopic assemblies in mTECs lacking PLK4 (Figure 5E–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: γTubulin formed ectopic assemblies in mTECs lacking PLK4.
source: The distal centriole protein Centrobin, the distal appendage component CEP164 and γTubulin also formed ectopic assemblies in mTECs lacking PLK4 (Figure 5E–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The centriole cartwheel components STIL and SAS6 did not form detectable assemblies in PLK4F/F;R26Cre mTECs.
source: However, the centriole cartwheel components STIL and SAS6, and the PCM component CDK5RAP2 did not form detectable assemblies in PLK4F/F;R26Cre mTECs (Figure 5G, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The PCM component CDK5RAP2 did not form detectable assemblies in PLK4F/F;R26Cre mTECs.
source: However, the centriole cartwheel components STIL and SAS6, and the PCM component CDK5RAP2 did not form detectable assemblies in PLK4F/F;R26Cre mTECs (Figure 5G, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: At ALI 7, ~35% of control Sas4F/+;R26Cre mTECs were multiciliated.
source: At ALI 7–35% of control Sas4F/+;R26Cre mTECs were multiciliated, while ~18% of Sas4F/F;R26Cre mTECs formed MCCs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: At ALI 7, ~18% of Sas4F/F;R26Cre mTECs formed MCCs.
source: At ALI 7–35% of control Sas4F/+;R26Cre mTECs were multiciliated, while ~18% of Sas4F/F;R26Cre mTECs formed MCCs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: 15% of Sas4F/F;R26Cre mTECs displayed filamentous assemblies of Centrin and spherical assemblies of CEP135 at ALI 7.
source: At the same time point, 15% of Sas4F/F;R26Cre mTECs displayed filamentous assemblies of Centrin and spherical assemblies of CEP135, a penetrance similar to that observed in mTECs lacking PLK4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: The elevated expression of centriole proteins in mTECs drives the formation of assemblies of specific centriole components when centriole amplification is prevented.
source: These data suggest that the elevated expression of centriole proteins in mTECs drives the formation of assemblies of specific centriole components when centriole amplification is prevented.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: Treatment with 1.5 µM of centrinone failed to block procentriole production in ependymal cells.
source: A previous study reported that treatment with 1.5 µM of the PLK4 inhibitor centrinone failed to block procentriole production in ependymal cells (Zhao et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The levels of PLK4 progressively increased in ependymal cells treated with ≥2.5 μM centrinone.
source: The levels of PLK4 progressively increased in ependymal cells treated with ≥2.5 μM centrinone (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in a figure.

claim: At doses above 2.5 µM centrinone, there was a progressive decline in the fraction of MBB and disengagement (D) phase cells and an increase in the fraction of cells in amplification (A) or growth (G) phase.
source: At doses above 2.5 µM, we also observed a progressive decline in the fraction of MBB and disengagement (D) phase cells and an increase in the fraction of cells in amplification (A) or growth (G) phase (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Cells that reached MBB phase in the presence of 5 µM or 10 µM centrinone contained fewer centrioles than controls.
source: Moreover, cells that reached MBB phase in the presence of 5 µM or 10 µM centrinone contained fewer centrioles than controls (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Treatment with 1 μM of centrinone does not perturb centriole amplification in mTECs.
source: Previous work shows that treatment with 1 μM of centrinone does not perturb centriole amplification in mTECs (Nanjundappa et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: 10 μM centrinone did not change the percentage of multiciliated mTECs at ALI 7, or the number of centrioles made per cell.
source: 10 μM centrinone did not change the percentage of multiciliated mTECs at ALI 7, or the number of centrioles made per cell (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: There was no increase in PLK4 abundance on deuterosomes in mTECs treated with 1–10 µM of centrinone.
source: However, there was no increase in PLK4 abundance on deuterosomes in mTECs treated with 1–10 µM of centrinone, a hallmark of kinase inhibition in cycling cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2D, E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Tracheal epithelial cells express high levels of P-glycoprotein (Pgp) efflux pumps.
source: Tracheal epithelial cells express high levels of P-glycoprotein (Pgp) efflux pumps (Florea et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Pgp efflux pumps confer multidrug resistance.
source: Given that Pgp efflux pumps confer multidrug resistance, it is plausible that centrinone is actively pumped out of mTECs.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Verapamil alone reduced the percentage of multiciliated mTECs at ALI 7.
source: While Verapamil alone reduced the percentage of multiciliated mTECs at ALI 7, the number of centrioles produced in multicliated cells was unchanged (Figure 6—figure supplement 2F, G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The number of centrioles produced in multiciliated cells was unchanged by Verapamil alone.
source: While Verapamil alone reduced the percentage of multiciliated mTECs at ALI 7, the number of centrioles produced in multicliated cells was unchanged (Figure 6—figure supplement 2F, G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Treatment with 10 μM centrinone and Verapamil reduced the number of centrioles in MCCs to approximately half that observed in cells treated with 10 μM of centrinone alone.
source: Treatment with 10 μM centrinone and Verapamil reduced the number of centrioles in MCCs to approximately half that observed in cells treated with 10 μM of centrinone alone (Figure 6—figure supplement 2F, G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Drug efflux pumps may serve to reduce the effective intracellular concentration of centrinone in mTECs.
source: This suggests that drug efflux pumps may serve to reduce the effective intracellular concentration of centrinone in mTECs.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: PLK4 abundance on deuterosomes was ~3.5-fold higher in Plk4cKD/F;R26Cre mTECs.
source: PLK4 abundance on deuterosomes was ~3.5-fold higher in Plk4cKD/F;R26Cre mTECs (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: 4OHT treatment had no impact on centriole amplification in Plk4cWT/F;R26Cre mTECs.
source: While 4OHT treatment had no impact on centriole amplification in Plk4cWT/F;R26Cre mTECs, Plk4cKD/F;R26Cre mTECs possessed large Centrin filaments and few procentrioles.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation.

claim: Plk4cKD/F;R26Cre mTECs possessed large Centrin filaments and few procentrioles.
source: While 4OHT treatment had no impact on centriole amplification in Plk4cWT/F;R26Cre mTECs, Plk4cKD/F;R26Cre mTECs possessed large Centrin filaments and few procentrioles.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation.

claim: 50% of Plk4cWT/F;R26Cre mTECs nucleated multicilia.
source: Moreover, while 50% of Plk4cWT/F;R26Cre mTECs nucleated multicilia, less than 5% of Plk4cKD/F;R26Cre mTECs contained basal bodies and nucleated multicilia by ALI 7 (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Less than 5% of Plk4cKD/F;R26Cre mTECs contained basal bodies and nucleated multicilia by ALI 7.
source: Moreover, while 50% of Plk4cWT/F;R26Cre mTECs nucleated multicilia, less than 5% of Plk4cKD/F;R26Cre mTECs contained basal bodies and nucleated multicilia by ALI 7 (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: PLK4 kinase activity is required to drive centriole biogenesis in mTECs.
source: These data show that PLK4 kinase activity is required to drive centriole biogenesis in mTECs.
evidence: The claim is based on the interpretation of experimental data.

claim: PLK4 was present on the deuterosomes of almost all Cre+ Plk4cKD/F ependymal cells.
source: PLK4 was present on the deuterosomes of almost all Cre+ Plk4cKD/F ependymal cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 4A).
